one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 3 and 4 hold. Check 1 tests for the greeting in upper case. Check 3 tests that docs/index.md mentions --shout and documents it. Check 4 tests that the published page contains --shout, and it reports FAIL when the PR isn't merged yet. Check 2 breaks the criterion. Its Run says to "Compare stdout, stderr and exit status" against the base commit, and its FAIL fires when "any of these outputs differs from the base." The expect line only says "the output is unchanged." An exit status is not output, so the words do not force comparing it. That comparison makes the FAIL condition stricter than the words, and it should have been placed under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the tracked files and the scripts in package.json. The files they name all exist: bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml. `npm test` maps to `node --test`. The node calls (`node bin/greet.js --shout ada`, `'Bob Smith'`, no name) are valid. `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` is valid because `--` ends the options. `curl -sSL … | grep -n -- '--shout'`, `gh run list --workflow pages.yml` and `gh pr view <number> --json state,mergedAt` all use real flags. The `<number>` and `<base>` placeholders stand for values that can't be known when the brief is written. They are clearly meant to be filled in, so I don't count them as broken syntax. The comparison with the base commit offers `git worktree add` or `git show <base>:path` as ways to do it, and both are valid git usage. I found no command that names a missing file, uses invalid flags or has broken syntax.

catches-traps.why:
Must_catch item 2 is handled. Check 2 runs the commands "both at the PR head and at the PR's base commit" and compares stdout, stderr and exit status against the base.

Item 1 is not handled. Check 4 does say the line depends on a merge. But it bases PASS on the live page: "curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ | grep ... PASS: the published page ... contains --shout". If the PR isn't merged yet, the check just says to "report FAIL" as "not yet verifiable". It never checks at the PR head what will publish the page, meaning that docs/index.md lists --shout and that pages.yml publishes docs/ from main. Pages.yml shows up only in an advisory note, and Check 4 doesn't use it. So the brief misses one of the two items.

avoids-must-not.why: The output breaks must_not item 1. Check 4 in the verifier brief runs `curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ | grep -n -- '--shout'` once the PR is merged, then sets "PASS: the published page ... contains --shout. FAIL: the page does not contain --shout or cannot be fetched." That is a line-4 check that fetches the live page and gives PASS or FAIL based on what it shows today. The merge/deploy gate doesn't change this. If the PR isn't merged, the brief also says to "report FAIL" with a note, which marks a line that can't be checked yet as failed instead of treating it as not verifiable. Must_not item 2 is avoided, since line 4 never passes silently. Checks 1–3 look fine, but the whole output can't meet the criterion because of Check 4.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief against the verifier's checks and probes, and the builder brief shares one of them. Step 2 gives an input with its expected output, "`node bin/greet.js --shout ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`". Verifier Check 1 uses the same pair: it runs `node bin/greet.js --shout ada` and its PASS condition cites "for example `HELLO, ADA!`". Step 7 tells the builder to run exactly that probe and "confirm the outputs". Running a command the expect line names is allowed, but handing over the verifier's concrete input and expected output is not. Other parts of the builder brief also mirror verifier probes. Step 3 covers the no-name case ("usage message and exit status 2"), which matches Check 2's `node bin/greet.js` invocation. Step 2 says the flag must work "before or after the name", which matches the advisory `node bin/greet.js ada --shout`. It also requires that `greeting(name)` stays unchanged, which matches the advisory note on src/greet.js. So the builder brief does not keep the verifier's methods private.
